title: B'nai Brith calls on Canadian universities to act after new campus antisemitism report
description: B’nai Brith Canada on Thursday called on universities across Canada to take immediate action after new research found that 42% of surveyed students witnessed at least one antisemitic event during the academic year. “These findings are profoundly disturbing,” said B’nai Brith Canada CEO Simon Wolle. “They suggest that some of the most historically dangerous expressions of antisemitism are being dismissed and/or accepted within the very institutions entrusted with educating Canada’s next generation.” The research, titled “Campus Antisemitism and Student Experiences II,” conducted by the Association for Canadian Studies and available on Canada’s government website, also revealed that 55% of responding students did not consider the statement that “Jews have too much influence on the economy” to be antisemitic. Thirty-nine percent did not consider the claim that the Holocaust is a myth or exaggerated to be antisemitic. "When deeply rooted antisemitic stereotypes are permeating through Canadian campuses, we have a serious problem," B’nai Brith Canada said in a statement. "These findings are a clear wake-up call that current efforts to address antisemitism on Canadian campuses are falling short." Despite accounting for only 1% of the Canadian population, Jewish Canadians were the targets of 71% of reported religiously motivated hate crimes in 2025.

title: Protesters briefly disrupt Israeli conductor's Brussels concert
description: Anti-Israel protesters in Belgium briefly disrupted a concert featuring Israeli conductor Lahav Shani on Tuesday, about a month after he publicly said he had “serious ethical questions” about Israel’s actions in Gaza. Activists shouted and threw leaflets from a balcony as the music began at Brussels' Bozar venue, which had resisted calls to cancel the event, De Standaard reported. Shani and his Munich Philharmonic nonetheless received applause and a standing ovation at the end of the concert. Approximately 65 protesters gathered outside the venue, accusing Shani of helping Israel whitewash what they described as genocide in Gaza, the paper also reported. Shani, who had faced earlier boycotts in Belgium, wrote an op-ed in the left-wing Haaretz daily last month in which he urged “compassion” with Gazans, lambasted Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and wrote that “turning a blind eye to settler violence, or even encouraging it, is a grave moral failure that endangers Israel's future as a legitimate democracy.” In September 2025, Belgium's Ghent Festival of Flanders canceled a performance by Shani and the Munich Philharmonic, citing “insufficient clarity” about his position toward Israel's government. Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever subsequently traveled to Essen, Germany, to attend a performance by Shani in a public gesture of support. title: Huckabee: Sanctioning Jews for Judea and Samaria construction is 'insanity'
description: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee said on Tuesday that a Wall Street Journal op-ed by legal scholar Eugene Kontorovich exposed the "crass hypocrisy" and "insanity" of sanctioning people for building homes in Judea and Samaria. Huckabee called it a "powerful essay" in an X post sharing the article, which was published on Monday. Kontorovich, a professor at George Mason University's Antonin Scalia Law School and a senior legal fellow at Advancing American Freedom, argued that such sanctions amount to an endorsement of Palestinian leaders' vision of "an apartheid-like state without Jews." He pointed to Palestinian Authority leader Mahmoud Abbas's statement that in such a proposed state "we would not see the presence of a single Israeli ... on our lands," and noted that Palestinian law bans Jewish land ownership. "Those who embrace coexistence of Arabs and Jews in Israel should demand nothing less from the Palestinians," Kontorovich wrote. The piece came days after House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries expressed support for advancing the West Bank Settler Violence Protection and Prevention Act, which would authorize sanctions and visa bans against those who commit acts of violence that undermine "peace, security or stability" in Judea and Samaria. In an interview with The New York Times published on Saturday, Jeffries said he supports advancing the bill within the new Congress' first 100 days. "I believe we should move on it early in the new Congress," he said, describing the measure as a step toward improving conditions on the ground and advancing "two states for two people." title: Indian travel agents meet counterparts in Jerusalem ahead of Air India's return to Israel
description: Israel's Tourism Ministry hosted a delegation of 12 leading Indian travel agents in Jerusalem for meetings with Israeli tour operators this week, as part of an effort to restore tourism ties ahead of Air India's planned resumption of flights next month, the ministry said on Tuesday. The event at the King David Hotel, which the ministry described as a "first-of-its-kind professional gathering," was held in cooperation with the Israel Incoming Tour Operators Association. "Through a series of one-on-one business meetings, participants established direct professional connections, explored tourism packages tailored to Indian travelers and laid the groundwork for resuming regular business activity and restoring visitor traffic from India to Israel as soon as possible," according to the press release. The Israeli Tourism Ministry's office in Mumbai recently signed a memorandum of understanding with the Travel Agents Association of India, and the ministry continues to invest in trade exhibitions, media campaigns and outreach to India's growing luxury travel market, it said. "India is a strategic partner of Israel and a friendly country with which we enjoy excellent relations," said Michael Izhakov, the ministry's director general. "The resumption of Air India's direct flights this coming December will be a significant force multiplier, enabling more and more tourists from India to come here easily and experience everything Israel has to offer," he added.

title: Kishinev teens attend European CTeen Shabbaton
description: Jewish teens from the Kishinev CTeen/EnerJew chapter in Moldova returned home after participating in the European CTeen Shabbaton in Paris, held Nov. 19 to 22. More than 800 teens from some 400 schools in 30 countries participated in the weekend, organized by CTeen International, the youth arm of the worldwide Chabad movement, in cooperation with Chabad of Paris and CTeen France. Rabbi Shneur Zalman Tifenbrun, a Chabad rabbi in Kishinev, led the Kishinev delegation. On Saturday night, some 1,500 Jewish teens gathered on the Champ de Mars at the foot of the Eiffel Tower for a public celebration of Jewish pride. Participants marked the end of Shabbat with an outdoor Havdalah ceremony, recited Shema in unison while holding flags representing their home countries, and prayed for peace and the safety of Jewish communities worldwide. Teens from Kishinev carried the Moldovan flag during the gathering. A large screen displayed the message "WELCOME CTEEN MOLDOVA," along with a photograph of the Kishinev delegation and the Moldovan coat of arms, as part of a presentation featuring delegations from participating countries. CTeen operates more than 900 chapters in more than 60 countries. The Shabbaton provided an opportunity for Jewish teens, including participants who are the only Jewish students in their classes, to meet peers from other countries and take part in shared Jewish experiences. The Kishinev delegation returned home with new friendships and experiences from the international gathering.

title: Israel advances 1,515 housing units in Samaria
description: The Supreme Planning Council of the Israeli Defense Ministry's Civil Administration is advancing plans for 1,515 housing units in Samaria, including the first assisted-living facility of its kind in the area, Channel 14 News reported on Sunday. In the western Samaria community of Karnei Shomron, a plan for 436 housing units will be advanced, alongside a 250-unit assisted-living facility, according to the report. In nearby Etz Efraim, in the Samaria Regional Council, a 192-unit plan will receive final approval. Meanwhile, in the Binyamin Regional Council community of Haresha, a plan for 637 units will receive final approval. Together with another approved plan, more than 900 units will be advanced in the community. "Judea and Samaria is no longer the backyard of the State of Israel, but the heart of the land and the state," Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who also serves as a minister in the Defense Ministry overseeing civilian affairs in Judea and Samaria, wrote on X on Monday, sharing the report. Blair, who sits on U.S. President Donald Trump's Board of Peace, which oversees the Gaza ceasefire, told The Sunday Times ' Matthew Syed that the U.N.-backed plan would replace Hamas with a new Palestinian government supported by the international community. "Whilst Hamas are there threatening Israel, Israel is going to continue to impose those restrictions," he said, adding that the aim was "to do the disarmament of Hamas in a way that gives confidence that as they disarm Israel withdraws." Blair called the plan "perfectly sensible," adding, "We have just got to be given a chance to make it work." He also described the central struggle across the Middle East as one between those who want tolerant societies and those who seek to turn Islam into a political ideology, saying the Arab-Israeli conflict has "that element also to it because of Hamas, which is part of the Muslim Brotherhood." Blair said he remains optimistic about the prospects for peace, while acknowledging that his views on democracy in the region have become more "nuanced" since his time in office. title: Dutch right-wing party expels six members over neo-Nazi ties
description: A Dutch political party kicked out six members on Thursday following a televised exposé that tied them to neo-Nazi gatherings, including one on Adolf Hitler’s birthday, where participants burned books one of them described as being "Jewish." The right-wing Forum for Democracy (FvD), founded by Thierry Baudet in 2016 and currently led by Lidewij de Vos, announced the expulsions following the airing on Wednesday of a news report by the Dutch television program Zembla . The investigation showed men participating in cage fights at locations in the Netherlands. Hidden camera footage showed participants and spectators performing Nazi salutes. Two members of the party's youth organization took part in fights. At the gathering in Luxembourg commemorating Hitler's birthday, members of the neo-Nazi group Wolvenrad burned books that Zembla identified as works by Jewish authors. A participant remarked, "They're Jewish books, aren't they? Let's see whether there's any money hidden inside." The investigation identified participants associated with neo-Nazi organizations, including Active Club Dietsland, Hammerskins and Wolvenrad. title: Iran's top diplomat sets 'red lines' on uranium stockpile
description: Iran has "clear red lines" on its enriched uranium stockpile and will not allow the material to be taken out of the country, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in an interview published on Saturday by Iran Daily , an English-language newspaper of Tehran's state-run IRNA news agency. "I believe a formula can be found," Araghchi said about Iran's stockpile of 400 kilograms (about 880 pounds) of uranium enriched to 60%, adding that "the stockpile will be used according to our needs" and that the issue "cannot be decided in isolation from the others." Araghchi said the United States had rejected a two-day proposal under which Washington would fulfill its commitments on the first day and the Islamic Republic would reopen the Strait of Hormuz on the second, when negotiations on a final agreement would begin. "The two-day plan is no longer on the table," he said, adding that Tehran's "seven conditions must be met before the Strait reopens." Araghchi said Tehran was seeking a "good, honorable and dignified agreement." Addressing calls to change Iran's nuclear doctrine, he said, "For now, our doctrine has not changed, and our official position remains the same." Iran has maintained that its nuclear program is strictly peaceful while it has continued to ramp up its uranium enrichment. In recent years, the regime has claimed that Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, who was killed in the opening strike of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, issued a fatwa, or religious edict, outlawing weapons of mass destruction.

title: Israeli Diaspora Ministry: Viral video of Jewish youth raiding Palestinian plantation is AI fake
description: Israel's Ministry of Diaspora Affairs and Combating Antisemitism told JNS on Sunday that a viral video purporting to show Jewish "hilltop youth" stealing bananas and damaging equipment at a Palestinian plantation near Nablus (Shechem) in Samaria was generated using artificial intelligence and presented as authentic to reinforce anti-Israel narratives. "The video in question garnered over 1.5 million views in a short period, despite having been generated using AI. The concern is that viewers will encounter this content, believe it to be genuine footage, and share it further, thereby disseminating false information," the ministry said in a statement to JNS. According to the ministry's investigation, the clip first appeared on X on Nov. 16. It was then spread further by anti-Israel accounts based in the United States, Brazil, Turkey, Qatar and Pakistan, including one with about 774,000 followers. Some of the accounts are suspected of being bots. The video appears to have been created in response to Palestinian media reports, which have not been independently verified, alleging damage to banana plantations in the Nablus area, the ministry said. The ministry told JNS it monitors social media, uses technological tools to identify AI-generated fakes and publishes its findings in order to identify fabricated content early and mitigate the damage to public perception. "Videos fabricated using AI technologies are a destructive weapon in the battle for public opinion against Israel," Diaspora Affairs Minister Amichai Chikli said in a separate statement. "We will not allow lies to become truth."
